claims.claim: South Branch Lake (Penobscot County), 1971–72: nesting success 67 % and 77 %, an average of 3,943 fry rising from each nest; a fall in water level the main cause of the poorer 1971 season; egg mortality highest under males shorter than 400 mm with large egg deposits; fanning lowered sac-fry but not egg mortality (Neves 1975, abstract)
claims.note: No abstract was reachable either (Crossref has none; OpenAlex is out of allowance today), so not even the abstract-level statement was re-seen. Forbes 1981 (Table 1) relays 67–68 % for South Branch Lake (15–30 nests), not 67 and 77 %: see notes.

notes: A Maine primary source the paper leans on for its only Maine smallmouth nest data; worth a library copy (TAFS 104(1): 83–87). A DISCREPANCY to settle when it is read: Forbes (1981, a Wisconsin DNR review; read on its page image, Table 1, printed p. 4, PDF p. 5 — indexed here as Neves_1975.Forbes1981) relays South Branch Lake as 67–68 % of nests producing fry, from 15–30 nests studied, whereas the paper (§3.6.2) and config.js:488 say 67 % and 77 % (from the abstract, seen second-hand). They cannot both be right. The project's note (Whole lake 3D fish simulation/egg_stage.md, line 166) quotes the abstract as '67% and 77%, respectively', so Forbes's 67–68 may be the slip, but the note's quote is unverified here; until the article is read, give "67–68 % (Neves 1975, via Forbes 1981)" or flag it. Forbes also relays from Neves: nests 0.8 m deep and 0.6 m in diameter, on coarse gravel with fist-sized rubble, and that unguarded nests fail (Forbes pp. 2–4). None of this confirms the article.
